correctness.rationale: All integers n>=2 and 1<=k<n. Periodic k-sets have vanishing first cyclic root moment, but one-coordinate exchanges have nonzero moment difference, so no two periodic words are Johnson-adjacent. Every unforced fixed-weight trace fiber contains a Johnson edge; the only forced positive/negative traces occur at |S|=min(k,n-k) and require primitive support. At top rank the omitted facets are pairwise ridge-disjoint; each missing attaching boundary already bounds the cone of the other facets in a rank-(r+1) simplex, so its attachment is null. Simplex skeleton homotopy then yields the integral sphere wedge; r=1 is handled separately. The standalone checker exhausted 81,924 support instances through n=12 and 45 GF(2) top boundaries through n=10; computations are finite corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: Primitive fixed-density necklace ensembles are natural objects, and the exact all-support query behavior is structurally different from counting their members. The arithmetic restriction removes only mutually non-ridge-adjacent top facets while leaving every smaller support. The resulting complete shattering polynomial, dimension and precise integral homotopy class are motivated, infinite-family invariants with clear relevance to learning theory and simplicial combinatorics; neither the Möbius count nor a direct relabeling alone produces this conclusion.
